topics.title: Warming winters challenge cranberry growers
topics.summary: Cranberry-growing regions have gained an average of 14 warmer winter days since 1970, bringing unpredictable thaw-and-freeze cycles for a classic holiday crop.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a favorite seasonal food became harder to grow, would you try substitutes, pay more for the original, or start a new tradition?

topics.title: CBeebies heads to Netflix
topics.summary: The BBC will trial a CBeebies hub on Netflix for six months, putting 24 preschool shows, including Teletubbies and Hey Duggee, before more families worldwide.
topics.discussionPrompt: Do you like finding everything in one streaming place, or does it feel better when a favorite show has its own special home?

topics.title: Children’s Booker unveils eight finalists
topics.summary: The inaugural Children’s Booker Prize announced an eight-book shortlist. Four child judges will join the panel before the winner is named in February.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you were judging a kids’ book prize, what would matter most: the funniest character, the best adventure, beautiful writing, or a story you cannot stop thinking about?

topics.title: Artists press for AI copyright safeguards
topics.summary: More than 7,000 artists, including Kate Bush and Grace Jones, urged Australia to preserve copyright protections as lawmakers consider AI-related reforms.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an AI learned from your drawings, songs, or stories, what kind of credit or permission would feel fair to you?

topics.title: Australian science prizes honor medical research
topics.summary: Australia’s Prime Minister’s Prizes for Science recognized Georgina Long’s work improving melanoma survival rates and physicist Anthony Thomas’s research.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which kind of breakthrough would you most like to cheer on: medicine, space, climate solutions, or a discovery that makes daily life easier?

topics.title: Sweden weighs data-centre growth
topics.summary: New reporting explores how Sweden’s expanding data-centre sector is stirring debate over energy, land use, local benefits and the infrastructure behind digital life.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you welcome a huge data centre nearby if it brought jobs, or would you first want answers about power, water, and the neighborhood?

topics.title: School bus drivers are in short supply
topics.summary: US school districts are grappling with fewer bus drivers, with low pay and difficult working conditions cited as key pressures on a familiar community service.
topics.discussionPrompt: What everyday job deserves more appreciation because so many routines quietly depend on it running smoothly?

topics.title: Compass plans New York listing
topics.summary: Food-services company Compass confirmed plans to move its main stock-market listing from London to New York, a notable shift for a major British business.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a hometown company moved its main headquarters or stock listing abroad, would it change how local people feel about it?

topics.title: Beatles attraction plan meets noise concern
topics.summary: A proposed Beatles attraction on London’s Savile Row faces a restriction on rooftop gigs, reopening a playful debate about preserving a famous music moment.
topics.discussionPrompt: Should famous places be kept quiet and protected, or should they host lively events that let new people make memories there?

topics.title: Tech shares slide again
topics.summary: Technology shares fell in premarket trading, with investors focused on the AI sector and the ripple effects of fresh developments around Nvidia.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new technology becomes everyone’s favorite investment, what signs tell you excitement is healthy versus getting a little carried away?
